requirements.requirement: Allow node2 (lan-a) to reach node3 (lan-b) on TCP port 5432
requirements.summary: VyOS forward filter rule 10 (tcp dport 5432, eth1 to eth2) committed and saved. Direct test: nc listener on node3:5432 received hello payload sent from node2, rule 10 counter incremented to 1 packet. Re-verified identically after all three node restarts, with final counter at 3 packets.

requirements.requirement: Reject all other traffic between lan-a and lan-b (node2 to node3)
requirements.summary: Default-action drop plus rule 900 explicit reject-all was committed. Directly tested: node2 to node3 ICMP ping rejected (port-unreachable), node2 to node3 TCP/22 connection-refused, node3 to node2 TCP/22 connection-refused, all reproduced again after all three restarts with rule 900 counter incrementing to 5. ICMP from node3 to node2 direction specifically was not separately tested, but the symmetric TCP/22 test plus the deny-all default action provide strong coverage.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (independent of public contract)
requirements.summary: All three nodes show pre-restart boot_id, a reboot acknowledgement, connection loss during the transition, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and re-verified recovered state (firewall ruleset/interfaces for node1; ens7 IP+route for node2/node3) plus a functional re-test of the allow/reject policy after each restart. This matches the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity cross-check, which shows differing boot IDs for all three nodes.

overall_summary: Both material firewall outcomes are directly demonstrated with live traffic tests and counter evidence: TCP/5432 from node2 to node3 succeeds, and all other cross-LAN traffic (ping, TCP/22 in both directions) is rejected via default-drop plus an explicit reject-all rule. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was completed for all three nodes with pre/post boot-identity changes, restart acknowledgements, and confirmed recovery of both connectivity and the firewall/routing configuration, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good overall; the only flaw is a small leftover temp pid/log file on node3 from the final connectivity test.
limitations: ICMP/ping from node3 to node2 direction specifically was not tested (only TCP/22 in that direction and ping in the node2 to node3 direction were tested), though the deny-all default-action and rule 900 counter make this a low-risk gap.

Preparation phase was disabled/static (prepare.enabled=false) and after_prepare is an alias of before_prepare, so no independent preparer-baseline distinct from initial state could be used for hygiene comparison beyond before_prepare vs after_executor.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were largely read-only discovery (interface/route/os checks, VyOS template/xml searches for firewall syntax) or directly contributed to the task (interface addressing, static routes, firewall rule configuration, nc-based connectivity tests, and the mandatory restart cycle). A few VyOS firewall set attempts failed validation (e.g. cmd-ce04ccf596d8419b state established enable / state related enable) but did not commit or leave residue, since the executor corrected syntax before the final commit. One unreverted residue: temporary nc listener log/pid files (/tmp/nc5432d.log, /tmp/nc5432d.pid) were left on node3, visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot; the nc process was killed in cmd-2746cf0ac0214423 but the pid/log files created in cmd-b8ccb44472704af9 were not removed. This is a minor, bounded, non-security-impacting leftover.
